A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPT-based account of black swans in stationary environments, despite retitling and substantial reorganization. The main text, figures, equations, references and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical constructions, worked hypothetical examples and proofs. Historical and psychological observations are attributed to other work; no original experiments, simulations or data analyses are reported.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical, including Appendices A–G. Its mathematical case studies and cited real-world examples do not constitute original empirical results.

M1.justification: The three-MDP perception/estimation framework and CPT distortions remain. The separately named distorted MDP describes the existing transition-distortion case, and Algorithm 1 restates v1's spatial-black-swan classification rather than introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or benchmarks for training or evaluation. Additional real-world examples in v2's introduction are cited motivation, not expanded evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates competing methods. The added discussion of distributional RL and other approaches changes related work, not an experimental comparator set.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. The MDP horizons, state counts and reward restrictions concern theoretical constructions; their revisions belong under T1.

E4.justification: v1's Examples 2–3, worked lottery cases examining rare-event neglect and preference reversal, are removed. The insurance example and the bandit, two-state and three-state theoretical case studies remain. This reduces analytical case-study support, without changing empirical robustness evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The theoretical concentration-bound derivation remains in v2's Appendix F despite its removal from the main theorem statement.

E6.justification: Removing v1's lottery examples removes their calculated outcomes, including the 0.0005% adverse-event probability and true utility of -1 versus perceived utility of -0.2. These are analytical illustrations, not measured performance. The retained insurance example's -10 versus -15 comparison is unchanged.

T1.justification: The five main theorem arguments largely survive, but some formal content changes. v2's Proposition 2 replaces v1's Proposition 3 universal reward-interval assertion with a sufficient-condition formulation. The subjective rationality axioms and risk-set limit in v1 Equation (10) disappear. The dedicated terminal-reward/Bellman setup is also omitted, although v2's Appendix F still invokes its reward assumption.

C1.justification: The central claim that misperception permits black swans in stationary environments remains. Hypothesis 1 changes from attributing black swans to spatial and temporal misperception to stating that misperception can cause them. v2 also explicitly extends its introductory argument to ML systems regardless of representation capacity or scalability.

C2.justification: v2 corrects the explanation of R < u−(R) from pessimistic perception to optimistic reward overestimation. It also explicitly interprets Theorem 5 as requiring more frequent perception correction for larger perception gaps and higher black-swan probabilities, and adds a mechanism-based critique of distributional RL.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies an implemented system, experimental hyperparameters, hardware requirements or code/data access instructions. The new notation table assists reading rather than adding implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around ML safety and existing black-swan approaches, adding discussion and citations concerning robustness, AutoML, out-of-distribution detection and black-swan prediction or mitigation. Section 7 adds a distributional-RL critique citing Bellemare et al. The earlier agency and non-stationary-RL background is reduced, while much existing safe-RL/CPT discussion survives in appendices.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites and reorganizes the narrative: preliminaries precede classification and case studies, related work receives a condensed main-text section, and substantial background and mathematical preparation move into appendices. The title and terminology change, including spatial black swans becoming S-BLACK SWAN and Universe MDP becoming ground truth MDP.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted with different typography, headings and title-page organization. v1's Figures 1 and 3 become a single four-panel Figure 1; the framework diagram becomes a smaller figure beside text. Appendix A adds a notation table spanning two pages. The merged diagrams retain their earlier substantive content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves navigation through reorganized preliminaries, consolidated figures and a notation table, and corrects the reward-overestimation explanation. However, v1's dedicated theoretical setup disappears while v2's retained proof still invokes its terminal-reward assumption through 'section ??'; other assumption and equation references also become unresolved. With the principal proof arguments unchanged, the accessibility gains and reduced mathematical traceability leave the net quality direction uncertain.
